summary.goal: Compute attention signals from existing plan data to categorize plans by what needs human action.
summary.context: Attention signals derive from data already in the system. Backend computes these on list fetch; frontend receives pre-categorized results. This avoids N+1 queries and keeps logic centralized. Note: execution status and gate data come from the orchestrator (external service) - the planner handles this gracefully when orchestrator is unavailable.

acceptance_criteria.description: Backend /plans endpoint returns attention_types for each plan when queried with ?include_attention=true
Attention types: awaiting_approval, change_request, gate_pending, execution_failed, unread_comments, stale_draft, active, none
awaiting_approval: draft with submitted_at set (waiting for reviewer)
change_request: has pending ChangeRequest from orchestrator
gate_pending: published plan with execution blocked on human_approval gate
execution_failed: published plan with failed execution status
unread_comments: plan has unresolved comments on latest version
stale_draft: draft not updated in >7 days (configurable threshold)
active: draft updated within last 24h OR published with running execution
Plans can have multiple attention types; API returns array
When orchestrator is unavailable, gate_pending and execution_failed signals are omitted (graceful degradation)

Config includes stale_draft_threshold_days (default 7) and active_threshold_hours (default 24).

acceptance_criteria.description: AttentionType enum exported with all 8 types: 'awaiting_approval' | 'change_request' | 'gate_pending' | 'execution_failed' | 'unread_comments' | 'stale_draft' | 'active' | 'none'
AttentionConfigSchema with stale_draft_threshold_days (number, default 7) and active_threshold_hours (number, default 24)
DEFAULT_ATTENTION_CONFIG exported with sensible defaults

steps.title: Implement computeAttentionTypes pure function
steps.description: Create computeAttentionTypes function that takes plan data and related context (changeRequests, executionStatus, unresolvedCommentCount) and returns AttentionType[]. This is a pure function with no side effects - all data is passed in.

acceptance_criteria.description: Function signature: computeAttentionTypes(input: AttentionInput, config?: AttentionConfig): AttentionType[]
AttentionInput type: { plan: Plan, latestVersion: PlanVersion, pendingChangeRequests: number, executionStatus?: ExecutionStatus | null, unresolvedCommentCount: number }
Returns 'awaiting_approval' when version.status === 'draft' AND version.submitted_at is set
Returns 'change_request' when pendingChangeRequests > 0
Returns 'gate_pending' when version.status === 'published' AND executionStatus has blocked step with gate
Returns 'execution_failed' when version.status === 'published' AND executionStatus.status === 'failed'
Returns 'unread_comments' when unresolvedCommentCount > 0
Returns 'stale_draft' when version.status === 'draft' AND updated_at older than threshold
Returns 'active' when (version.status === 'draft' AND updated_at within active threshold) OR (version.status === 'published' AND executionStatus.status === 'running')
Returns ['none'] if no other signals apply
Unit tests cover all 8 attention type conditions plus edge cases (multiple signals, null executionStatus)

steps.title: Add listPlansWithAttention to storage interface
steps.description: Extend PlanStorage interface with listPlansWithAttention method that returns plans with pre-joined data needed for attention computation (pending change request count, unresolved comment count per plan).

acceptance_criteria.description: PlanStorage interface has: listPlansWithAttention(status?: PlanStatus): PlanWithAttentionData[]
PlanWithAttentionData type: { plan: Plan, latestVersion: PlanVersion, pendingChangeRequestCount: number, unresolvedCommentCount: number }
SqliteStorage implements listPlansWithAttention using JOINs and subqueries (no N+1)

steps.title: Implement efficient SQL query for attention data
steps.description: Implement listPlansWithAttention in SqliteStorage using a single query with LEFT JOINs to change_requests and comments tables, aggregating counts. The query should fetch: plans joined with latest version, COUNT of pending change_requests per plan, COUNT of unresolved comments per (plan, latest_version).

acceptance_criteria.description: Single SQL query fetches all data (verified via EXPLAIN or query count logging)
Query uses subqueries or window functions to get latest version per plan
pending_change_request_count: COUNT of change_requests WHERE status = 'pending' AND plan_id matches
unresolved_comment_count: COUNT of comments WHERE resolved = 0 AND plan_id matches AND version = latest_version
Status filter still works: when status param provided, only returns plans with matching version status
Integration test verifies correct counts with test data

steps.title: Create orchestrator client for execution status batch fetch
steps.description: Create src/orchestrator/client.ts with getExecutionStatusBatch(planIds: string[]): Promise<Map<string, ExecutionStatus | null>>. This fetches execution status for multiple plans in a single call. Returns null for plans with no execution or when orchestrator is unavailable. Includes timeout and graceful error handling.

acceptance_criteria.description: Function: getExecutionStatusBatch(planIds: string[]): Promise<Map<string, ExecutionStatus | null>>
Makes single HTTP request to orchestrator batch endpoint: POST /executions/batch with { plan_ids: string[] }
Returns Map where key is plan_id, value is ExecutionStatus or null
On orchestrator error or timeout (default 5s), returns empty Map (no exceptions thrown to caller)
Logs warning when orchestrator unavailable for observability
ORCHESTRATOR_URL configurable via environment variable (default: none - disabled)

steps.title: Extend GET /plans endpoint with include_attention parameter
steps.description: Update plans.ts handler to support ?include_attention=true query param. When set, use listPlansWithAttention, fetch execution status batch from orchestrator, and compute attention_types for each plan using computeAttentionTypes.

acceptance_criteria.description: ListPlansQuerySchema extended with include_attention: z.boolean().optional()
When include_attention=false or omitted, response unchanged (backward compatible)
When include_attention=true, each PlanSummary includes attention_types: AttentionType[]
Response type: { plans: Array<PlanSummary & { attention_types?: AttentionType[] }> }
Orchestrator call is optional - if ORCHESTRATOR_URL not set or call fails, gate_pending and execution_failed signals omitted
Performance: entire flow completes in <500ms for 100 plans (excluding network latency to orchestrator)

PlanSummary extended: attention_types?: AttentionType[]
Types exported from @/types index
